terms.title: Product Launch
terms.summary: Coordinated release of a product or feature to a target audience.
terms.details: A launch connects planning, readiness, messaging, channel activation, measurement, and follow-up into one lifecycle.

terms.title: Go-To-Market Strategy
terms.summary: Plan for reaching the right audience with the right message and channel mix.
terms.details: The GTM strategy defines the target segment, positioning, launch channels, success metrics, and feedback loops.

terms.title: Launch Plan
terms.summary: Documented plan for launch activities, owners, dates, dependencies, and risks.
terms.details: The plan gives teams a shared operating view across launch readiness, campaigns, enablement, support, and measurement.

terms.title: Launch Owner
terms.summary: Person accountable for coordinating launch execution and tradeoff decisions.
terms.details: The launch owner keeps work moving across product, marketing, sales, support, and analytics.

terms.title: Product Manager
terms.summary: Person accountable for product direction, scope, and customer value.
terms.details: The product manager connects customer needs, business goals, launch scope, and roadmap decisions.

terms.title: Customer Segment
terms.summary: Group of customers with shared needs, behaviors, or buying triggers.
terms.details: Segments help teams tailor messaging, prioritization, onboarding, and success metrics.

terms.title: Target Persona
terms.summary: Representative user or buyer profile for launch planning.
terms.details: A persona makes audience assumptions explicit so messaging and channel choices can be tested.

terms.title: Positioning Statement
terms.summary: Concise explanation of who the product is for and why it matters.
terms.details: Positioning turns customer research into a clear claim that can be used across channels.

terms.title: Customer Objection
terms.summary: Concern or blocker that may prevent adoption.
terms.details: Objections inform messaging, enablement, support content, and readiness planning.

terms.title: Launch Channel
terms.summary: Surface used to reach, educate, or activate the target audience.
terms.details: Channels can include email, events, sales outreach, in-product messaging, partner motions, or community campaigns.

terms.title: Email Campaign
terms.summary: Outbound sequence used to announce, educate, or nurture customers.
terms.details: Email is often paired with landing pages, webinars, and sales follow-up.

terms.title: Webinar
terms.summary: Live or recorded session used to explain the launch and answer questions.
terms.details: Webinars help teams validate interest, capture objections, and generate qualified follow-up.

terms.title: Partner Motion
terms.summary: Launch path that reaches customers through partner sellers or ecosystems.
terms.details: Partner motions need clear enablement, shared messaging, and handoff rules.

terms.title: Launch Readiness Review
terms.summary: Checkpoint that confirms launch requirements are met.
terms.details: The review validates dependencies, risks, support coverage, channel readiness, and go/no-go criteria.

terms.title: Readiness Owner
terms.summary: Person responsible for confirming a readiness area is prepared.
terms.details: Readiness owners typically cover product, support, analytics, marketing, sales, and customer communications.

terms.title: Support Readiness
terms.summary: Preparation of support teams, docs, escalation paths, and known issues.
terms.details: Support readiness reduces launch risk and makes customer feedback actionable.

terms.title: Sales Enablement
terms.summary: Materials and guidance that help sellers explain and position the launch.
terms.details: Enablement can include talk tracks, objection handling, demos, FAQs, and target account guidance.

terms.title: Launch Milestone
terms.summary: Important date or checkpoint in the launch plan.
terms.details: Milestones coordinate dependent work such as content freeze, readiness review, channel activation, and post-launch analysis.

terms.title: Launch Risk
terms.summary: Potential issue that could delay, weaken, or confuse the launch.
terms.details: Risks should be assigned an owner, mitigation, due date, and review cadence.

terms.title: Success Metric
terms.summary: Measurement used to evaluate whether the launch met its goals.
terms.details: Metrics make outcomes observable and support post-launch learning.

terms.title: Adoption Funnel
terms.summary: Progression from awareness to trial, activation, and continued use.
terms.details: The funnel helps teams see where customers drop off and where launch improvements are needed.

terms.title: Adoption Rate
terms.summary: Share of the target audience that starts using the launched product or feature.
terms.details: Adoption rate is an early signal of reach, relevance, and activation success.

terms.title: Conversion Rate
terms.summary: Share of users who take a desired action after launch exposure.
terms.details: Conversion can measure signups, trial starts, registrations, qualified leads, or purchases.

terms.title: Qualified Lead
terms.summary: Prospect that meets agreed criteria for sales follow-up.
terms.details: Qualified leads connect channel activity to measurable pipeline and seller action.

terms.title: Retention Rate
terms.summary: Share of activated users who continue using the product over time.
terms.details: Retention helps distinguish launch curiosity from durable value.

terms.title: Feedback Loop
terms.summary: Mechanism for collecting launch feedback and turning it into improvements.
terms.details: Feedback loops connect support signals, customer research, metrics, and roadmap decisions.

terms.title: Post-Launch Review
terms.summary: Review that compares launch outcomes against goals and assumptions.
terms.details: The review captures lessons, metric movement, customer feedback, and follow-up actions.

terms.title: Roadmap
terms.summary: Sequenced view of future product direction and priorities.
terms.details: Launch outcomes should influence roadmap decisions when evidence supports a change.

terms.title: Landing Page
terms.summary: Web page that explains the launch offer and captures customer interest.
terms.details: Landing pages connect positioning, calls to action, tracking, and conversion goals.

terms.title: Call to Action
terms.summary: Prompt that asks the audience to take the next step.
terms.details: A CTA can ask people to register, start a trial, request a demo, read docs, or contact sales.

terms.title: Demo Script
terms.summary: Structured story used to show the product in a repeatable way.
terms.details: Demo scripts help presenters connect product behavior to customer pain and launch positioning.

terms.title: FAQ
terms.summary: Answers to expected customer, seller, support, or partner questions.
terms.details: FAQs reduce ambiguity and help teams respond consistently after launch.

terms.title: Release Notes
terms.summary: Concise description of what changed and what users should know.
terms.details: Release notes support customer communication, internal readiness, and post-launch support.

terms.title: Documentation
terms.summary: Guidance that helps users understand, adopt, and troubleshoot the launch.
terms.details: Documentation connects product details to onboarding, support, and success metrics.

terms.title: Awareness Stage
terms.summary: Point in the funnel where customers first learn about the launch.
terms.details: Awareness is usually driven by channels such as email, webinars, partners, and landing pages.

terms.title: Trial Stage
terms.summary: Point where customers evaluate the product through hands-on use.
terms.details: Trial stage metrics help teams understand whether launch traffic becomes meaningful product exploration.

terms.title: Activation Stage
terms.summary: Point where users complete the first meaningful product action.
terms.details: Activation shows whether users understand the value proposition well enough to start using it.

terms.title: Retention Stage
terms.summary: Point where customers keep using the product after the initial launch moment.
terms.details: Retention separates durable value from one-time curiosity.

terms.title: Customer Insight
terms.summary: Actionable learning about customer behavior, needs, or friction.
terms.details: Insights connect research, support feedback, and metrics to better launch decisions.

terms.title: Usage Signal
terms.summary: Observed behavior that indicates whether people are adopting the launch.
terms.details: Usage signals can include visits, trials, activations, repeat use, or feature engagement.

terms.title: Support Signal
terms.summary: Pattern from support tickets, questions, or escalations after launch.
terms.details: Support signals reveal confusion, missing docs, product issues, and objections that messaging did not resolve.

terms.title: Market Signal
terms.summary: External indication of customer, competitor, or category movement.
terms.details: Market signals help teams adapt positioning and prioritize channels.

terms.title: Dependency Risk
terms.summary: Risk caused by upstream work, systems, approvals, or teams not being ready.
terms.details: Dependency risks should have an owner, mitigation plan, and date tied to a launch milestone.

terms.title: Message Risk
terms.summary: Risk that the audience misunderstands or ignores the launch message.
terms.details: Message risk is reduced through customer research, positioning tests, and objection handling.

terms.title: Support Risk
terms.summary: Risk that support teams or materials are not ready for customer needs.
terms.details: Support risk can affect adoption, trust, and retention after launch.

terms.title: Measurement Risk
terms.summary: Risk that success cannot be evaluated clearly after launch.
terms.details: Measurement risk appears when metrics, baselines, instrumentation, or ownership are unclear.

terms.title: Positioning Test
terms.summary: Experiment that checks whether launch messaging is clear and compelling.
terms.details: A positioning test can compare claims, headlines, personas, or objection-handling language.

terms.title: Channel Test
terms.summary: Experiment that compares how different channels perform for the same audience.
terms.details: Channel tests help decide whether email, webinars, partners, or in-product surfaces deserve more investment.

terms.title: Onboarding Test
terms.summary: Experiment that checks whether users can reach first value.
terms.details: Onboarding tests expose activation friction before it becomes a retention problem.

terms.title: Pricing Test
terms.summary: Experiment that checks whether packaging or price blocks adoption.
terms.details: Pricing tests should be tied to a hypothesis, segment, measurement plan, and guardrails.

terms.title: Launch Standup
terms.summary: Recurring meeting that coordinates active launch work.
terms.details: Standups keep blockers, risks, milestones, and owners visible during launch execution.

terms.title: Workback Plan
terms.summary: Reverse timeline from launch date to required prep milestones.
terms.details: Workback plans help teams sequence content, readiness, review, and channel activation.

terms.title: Issue Triage
terms.summary: Process for prioritizing and routing launch problems.
terms.details: Triage connects support signals, launch risks, product fixes, and communications.

terms.title: Stakeholder Update
terms.summary: Concise status communication for launch sponsors and collaborators.
terms.details: Updates summarize progress, decisions, risks, metrics, and next actions.

terms.title: Onboarding Flow
terms.summary: Guided path that helps new users reach first value.
terms.details: Onboarding turns awareness and trial into activation by reducing setup friction.

terms.title: Baseline Metric
terms.summary: Pre-launch measurement used as a comparison point.
terms.details: Baselines make it possible to separate launch impact from normal variation.
